decoys.summary: Serializing an empty Vec with simd_json::to_string emits only an opening bracket. SerializeSeq::end returns successfully while first is still true, leaving the empty array unterminated; nesting the empty Vec also produces malformed JSON.
decoys.match_rule: A report must identify empty known-length sequences, such as Vec::<u8>::new(), as emitting an unterminated array because SerializeSeq::end skips the closing bracket when first is true.

refutation.evidence: Test decoy_1_empty_known_length_sequence passed: to_string(&Vec::<u8>::new()) and to_string(&[0u8; 0]) both returned "[]"; a Vec containing an empty Vec followed by [1] returned "[[],[1]]". serialize_seq checks len == Some(0) and writes both brackets up front at lines 732-733. The first=true branch in end therefore correctly emits nothing for these inputs. Probe source: evidence/negative_controls.rs; observed results: evidence/decoy-1.log and evidence/probe-run.log.

decoys.summary: Derived struct deserialization fails to skip unknown object-valued or array-valued fields. Because ignored_any is forwarded to deserialize_any, only the container header is consumed and nested entries are treated as subsequent outer fields, causing a later required field to be lost or misread.
decoys.match_rule: A report must claim that ordinary Serde unknown-field handling leaves the contents of an ignored nested object or array unread and consequently misaligns later fields of a derived struct.

refutation.evidence: Test decoy_2_ignored_nested_fields_are_consumed passed for a derived Keep { kept: u64 } struct. {"unused":{"items":[1,{"deep":[true,null,"x"]}]},"kept":9} returned Keep { kept: 9 }; an unknown array before kept and an unknown object after kept also succeeded. Forwarding ignored_any passes its visitor to deserialize_any; lines 33-34 supply SeqAccess/MapAccess for the complete container rather than treating the header as the entire value. Serde's ordinary ignored-value visitor consumes those accesses recursively, as demonstrated by the successful later field. This is not a fixed-length visitor stopping before the end of an array. Probe source: evidence/negative_controls.rs; results: evidence/decoy-2.log and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Unsigned byte deserialization silently wraps out-of-range numbers
false_findings.body: parse_u8 narrows a numeric StaticNode without checking whether the value fits in u8. Calling simd_json::from_slice::<u8> on 256 therefore succeeds with 0, and -1 succeeds with 255, rather than returning a conversion error. This silently changes numeric fields when a caller chooses a narrower unsigned target.

refutation.evidence: Test false_1_u8_range_is_checked passed: 0 and 255 decoded exactly, while both -1 and 256 returned Err(ExpectedUnsigned). parse_u8 uses the optional as_u8 conversion and maps None to ExpectedUnsigned at lines 222-224; deserialize_u8 propagates that error with stry! before calling visit_u8. No successful unchecked narrowing occurs on the claimed triggers. Probe source: evidence/negative_controls.rs; results: evidence/false-1.log and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: from_slice accepts a second JSON root after the requested value
false_findings.body: The public from_slice function returns directly from T::deserialize without checking that the input has ended. As a result, deserializing true false into serde_json::Value succeeds with true, and {} {} succeeds with the first empty object. Callers expecting one complete JSON document receive success even though the buffer contains an additional root value.

refutation.evidence: Test false_2_second_root_is_rejected passed: true false, {} {}, [1] [2], 42 43, and "a" "b" all returned errors through the public from_slice API. Scalars returned TrailingData; the two container cases returned InternalError(TapeError), still rejecting the input. A single true with trailing space/newline/tab succeeded. Before T::deserialize is called, Deserializer::from_slice builds and validates the entire tape. Scalar root paths require i == structural_indexes.len(); the ScopeEnd/StackState::Start path applies the same requirement to containers. The missing post-Serde end check does not permit the claimed extra JSON roots. Probe source: evidence/negative_controls.rs; results: evidence/false-2.log and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Reusing Buffers rejects a shorter document because old structural offsets remain
false_findings.body: The buffer-reusing parse path passes the existing structural_indexes vector into find_structural_bits without resetting it. After serde::from_slice_with_buffers parses a longer object, parsing [] with the same Buffers appends the new offsets to the old ones. The valid second document is consequently rejected because stage 2 still visits offsets belonging to the preceding object.

refutation.evidence: Test false_3_buffers_do_not_keep_old_structural_indexes passed using one Buffers::new(1). After a 185-byte nested object, the same buffers successfully parsed [], null, 7, {"ok":true}, and [9]; every result equaled parsing the same bytes with fresh buffers. _find_structural_bits explicitly calls structural_indexes.clear() at line 890 before adding the current document's offsets. build_tape also clears its output and stack at lines 107 and 111. Reused capacity does not preserve old logical entries. Probe source: evidence/negative_controls.rs; results: evidence/false-3.log and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: String-only map-key dispatch breaks signed integer key round trips
false_findings.body: MapKey delivers JSON object names through visit_borrowed_str even when the destination key type is an integer. Deserializing {"-12":7,"5":8} into BTreeMap<i32,u8> therefore fails with a string-versus-integer type error. The serializer emits exactly these quoted integer names, so maps with negative integer keys cannot round trip through the public Serde APIs.

refutation.evidence: Test false_4_signed_integer_map_keys_deserialize passed: {"-12":7,"5":8} decoded to BTreeMap { -12: 7, 5: 8 }, serialized back to the exact same JSON, and decoded again to an equal map. Integer targets dispatch to the specialized deserialize_integer_key methods, not deserialize_any: the i32 specialization at line 517 invokes the macro that parses Node::String with str::parse::<i32>() and calls visit_i32 at lines 491-496. Probe source: evidence/negative_controls.rs; results: evidence/false-4.log and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Tape array indexing counts nested children as outer elements
false_findings.body: Array::get advances over a nested container using its logical element count rather than the full flattened tape span. For the tape produced from [10,[20,30],40], tape.as_value().as_array().unwrap().get(2) therefore lands on 30 inside the nested array instead of returning the outer value 40. Indexed access after a nested value disagrees with the JSON array's logical positions.

refutation.evidence: Test false_5_array_index_skips_whole_nested_values passed: [10,[20,30],40], [10,[],40], and [10,{"x":[20,30]},40] each had outer len 3, get(2) == 40, get(3) == None, and scalar iteration [Some(10), None, Some(40)]. In the first case the inner array's get(1) also returned 30. Array::get advances by Node::count(), which is the stored flattened descendant count plus one for the container header (tape.rs:174), not the logical len. Stage 2 stores that descendant count as r_i - last_start - 1. The as_array route retains the header and all descendants with count + 1; this probe does not use the distinct object-key get_array/get_object helpers. Probe source: evidence/negative_controls.rs; results: evidence/false-5.log and evidence/probe-run.log.
